question.text: For some $\theta \in\left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$, let the eccentricity and the length of the latus rectum of the hyperbola $x^{2}-y^{2} \sec ^{2} \theta=8$ be $e_{1}$ and $l_{1}$, respectively, and let the eccentricity and the length of the latus rectum of the ellipse $x^{2} \sec ^{2} \theta+y^{2}=6$ be $e_{2}$ and $l_{2}$, respectively. If $e_{1}^{2}=e_{2}^{2}\left(\sec ^{2} \theta+1\right)$, then $\left(\frac{l_{1} l_{2}}{e_{1} e_{2}}\right) \tan ^{2} \theta$ is equal to $\_\_\_\_$
